standard.title: Specification for Ship's Snatch Blocks
standard.sector: Marine Engineering and Shipbuilding / Marine, Cargo Movement and Packaging

sectional_committee.name: Shipbuilding Sectional Committee
sectional_committee.number: MCPD 1 (formerly part of Mechanical Engineering Division Council)

standard.description: This standard specifies the material quality, general dimensions, tolerances, and proof test loads for ship's snatch blocks used with wire ropes corresponding to various safe working loads (SWL). Snatch blocks are defined as blocks designed with a hinged strap to enable the insertion of a wire rope onto the sheave at any position along the length of the rope.

certification.description: Voluntary Quality and Performance Specification. Since snatch blocks are marine outfitting cargo-handling components rather than consumer products, they are certified on a voluntary basis under the BIS ISI Certification scheme. However, compliance with IS 6140:1971 is universally required by marine surveyors, classification societies (such as IRS, LRS, or DNV-GL), the Indian Navy, and dock safety inspectors under Indian Dock Labour Regulations to approve shipboard cargo gear and rigging systems.
requirements: Every snatch block satisfying this standard may be legibly marked with the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) as a guarantee of quality and load-bearing safety.

Snatch blocks using wire ropes are strictly restricted to the following onboard operations: a) Deck lead blocks; b) Span blocks single or double reeved for topping an unloaded derrick; c) Lead blocks for guy tackle runners, provided the runner is turned to an angle of not more than 90°.
Specifies five standard block nominal sizes corresponding to safe working loads (SWL) and sheave sizes: Size 1 (150 mm cheek), Size 2 (200 mm), Size 3 (240 mm), Size 5 (320 mm), and Size 8 (400 mm).
The snatch block as a whole must be subjected to a static proof load test. The test load must be exactly four (4) times the declared Safe Working Load (SWL) of the block.
The proof test load must be applied and held continuously for a minimum period of five (5) minutes.

At the conclusion of the proof test, the snatch block must be disassembled, and all components must be carefully inspected for permanent deformation, cracks, or other structural defects. Blocks shall be approved subject to showing zero permanent deformation.
